title: Infections after kidney transplantation

steps.tx: Infectious vulnerability following kidney transplantation follows the **Fishman timeline**: Month **1** is dominated by nosocomial wound and surgical complications; Months **1** to **6** feature opportunistic viral and fungal pathogens; and beyond Month **6**, patients experience community-acquired pneumonia or chronic viral complications.

steps.tx: Primary **Cytomegalovirus** (**CMV**) infection presents the highest clinical risk in **CMV seronegative recipients** receiving kidneys from **CMV seropositive donors** (D+/R-). Without universal prophylaxis, patients develop severe invasive CMV disease, allograft endothelial injury, opportunistic superinfections, and heightened rates of acute cellular allograft rejection.

right.title: Moderate-Risk CMV Pair (R+)
points: Risk of viral reactivation or superinfection

steps.tx: Universal pharmacological prophylaxis against CMV utilizes oral **valganciclovir** (dose-adjusted for renal function), routinely continued for **6** months in high-risk **D+/R-** pairs and **3** months in CMV-seropositive recipients. For confirmed invasive tissue disease, intravenous **ganciclovir** remains the definitive first-line therapeutic agent across transplant centers.
steps.say: Universal pharmacological prophylaxis against CMV utilizes oral valganciclovir continued for 6 months in high-risk D+/R- pairs and 3 months in CMV-seropositive recipients. For confirmed invasive tissue disease, intravenous ganciclovir remains the definitive first-line therapeutic agent.

left.title: Clinical Sequence
points: Switch to IV ganciclovir if breakthrough tissue disease

steps.tx: Reactivation of latent **BK polyomavirus** (**BKPyV**) in renal allografts produces asymptomatic **viruria**, progressing to sustained **viremia** and destructive interstitial allograft nephritis. Routine prospective monthly screening using plasma **quantitative PCR** enables early detection of viral replication, prompting stepwise immunosuppression reduction before irreversible nephron loss occurs.

steps.tx: Definitive diagnosis of **BK virus nephropathy** requires allograft biopsy demonstrating viral cytopathic changes: enlarged tubular epithelial nuclei with basophilic **ground-glass viral inclusions**. Confirmatory diagnostic immunoperoxidase staining reveals intense nuclear expression of the **SV40 large T antigen** cross-reacting with BK polyomavirus capsids.

steps.tx: All solid organ transplant recipients require universal antimicrobial prophylaxis against **Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia** (**PJP**) using daily single-strength oral **trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole** for **3** to **6** months. This cost-effective regimen provides simultaneous secondary prophylaxis against bacterial urinary tract infections, systemic listeriosis, and pulmonary nocardiosis.

steps.tx: Life-threatening opportunistic **invasive fungal infections** (**Aspergillus fumigatus**, **Cryptococcus neoformans**, Mucorales) occur during periods of intensified antirejection immunosuppression. Triazole antifungals (**voriconazole**, posaconazole) are potent competitive inhibitors of hepatic microsomal **CYP3A4**, precipitating massive, dangerous elevations in therapeutic whole blood tacrolimus and cyclosporine concentrations.

rows: Requires urgent surgical debridement and amphotericin B

steps.tx: Administration of **live attenuated vaccines** (including **MMR**, **varicella**, **yellow fever**, and oral polio vaccine) is strictly **contraindicated** in kidney transplant recipients on maintenance immunosuppression. Due to impaired cell-mediated immunity, live viral strains can replicate unchecked, precipitating fulminant, fatal disseminated vaccine-strain infection.

left.title: Strictly Contraindicated Vaccines
points: Oral polio and live BCG vaccines

right.title: Recommended Inactivated Vaccines
points: Inactivated SARS-CoV-2 and Hepatitis B vaccines

steps.tx: **Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder** (**PTLD**) is driven mainly by **Epstein-Barr virus** (**EBV**). The highest risk is an EBV-seronegative recipient of an EBV-seropositive kidney. The growth is usually a B-cell lymphoproliferative clone. Reducing immunosuppression is the first treatment, and rituximab is added when the cells express CD20.
steps.say: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder is usually driven by Epstein-Barr virus. The highest risk is a recipient who has never met the virus and receives a kidney from a donor who has. Reducing immunosuppression is the first treatment, and rituximab is added when the B cells express CD20.

rows: Epstein-Barr virus driving a B-cell clone
Reduce immunosuppression, then rituximab if CD20 is present
